# French Pronounce

> A free interactive web tool to hear how French letters, accents, and common
> letter-combinations are pronounced. Click any tile to hear the exact sound and
> an example word spoken aloud in French. Built for beginners. No signup, no cost.

Site: https://frenchpronounce.com/

## What it covers
- The French alphabet (A–Z), each letter's name and pronunciation
- Common letter-combinations that trip up learners
- Accented letters: é, è, ê, à, ô, ç

## Key pronunciations (grapheme → sound → example)
- ou → /u/ ("oo" as in food) → bonjour
- oi → /wa/ ("wah") → moi
- au / eau → /o/ ("oh") → bateau
- ai / ei → /ɛ/ ("eh") → maison
- eu → /ø/ ("uh", rounded lips) → deux
- on / om → /ɔ̃/ (nasal "ong") → nom
- an / en → /ɑ̃/ (nasal "ahn") → enfant
- in / ain → /ɛ̃/ (nasal "ang") → pain
- un → /œ̃/ (nasal "uhn") → un
- ch → /ʃ/ ("sh") → chat
- gn → /ɲ/ ("ny" as in canyon) → montagne
- qu → /k/ → quatre
- ph → /f/ → photo
- ç → /s/ → français
- ille → /ij/ ("ee-y") → fille
- gu → /ɡ/ (hard g) → guitare
- é → /e/ ("ay", accent aigu) → café
- è → /ɛ/ ("eh", accent grave) → père
- ê → /ɛ/ ("eh", circonflexe) → être

## Notes
- The French "r" (/ʁ/) is pronounced at the back of the throat, not with the tongue tip.
- French has four nasal vowels: on, an, in, un.
- Many final consonants in French are silent.
- Audio uses the browser's built-in French text-to-speech voice.
